answer: Memory-hard seat seals. Each identity must hold its own 1 GiB table, built once from its public key with a slow memory-hard hash (about 40 s). Every epoch a beacon names 32 random leaves; the agent returns those leaves plus Merkle paths to its committed root, and a random verifier set (the oasis panel) rechecks them. Leaves are cut as 4 KiB timber blocks, so a delta of fresh blocks cannot be copied from a sibling. Cost uncaught: 1 GiB RAM held per fake, so 500 fakes need 500 GiB, and nothing can be pooled.
